truth_note: Intercept is the raw intercept at dose = 0 in the control arm
describe:
AutoBayes M0 model with categorical predictor(s) and interaction(s) (population-level only)
  formula   : y ~ dose + arm + dose:arm
  family    : gaussian, identity link
  data      : n = 240 observations, no group-level term (population-level model)
  arm       : categorical, treatment coding, reference 'control'; levels (sorted) control, high, low; coefficients b_arm[high, low]
              proportions among fitted rows: control 0.517, high 0.154, low 0.329

Linear predictor
  mu_i = a_c + (x_dose - mean(x_dose)) * b_dose + (1[arm_i = high] - p_arm[high]) * b_arm[high] + (1[arm_i = low] - p_arm[low]) * b_arm[low] + (x_dose * 1[arm_i = high] - q_dose:arm[high]) * b_dose:arm[high] + (x_dose * 1[arm_i = low] - q_dose:arm[low]) * b_dose:arm[low]
  b_arm[l] is the difference between level l and the reference 'control' on the response scale at dose = 0; at another value of dose the difference is b_arm[l] + dose * b_dose:arm[l], because the levels have different slopes. The reference has no coefficient.
  dose:arm: the reference level 'control' has the raw intercept a and slope b_dose; level l has intercept difference b_arm[l] and slope difference b_dose:arm[l], so its slope in dose is b_dose + b_dose:arm[l].
  Predictors are centred at their sample means (center_predictors=True, as in
  brms and Bambi); a dummy column's mean is its level's proportion p_z[l].
  Each product column x * 1[z = l] is centred at its OWN mean q, which is the level's proportion
  times the mean of x within that level: q_dose:arm[high] = -0.0972 = p_arm[high] 0.154 * mean(dose | arm = high) -0.6305 (not mean(dose) 0.2605 * p)
  times the mean of x within that level: q_dose:arm[low] = 0.3524 = p_arm[low] 0.329 * mean(dose | arm = low) 1.0706 (not mean(dose) 0.2605 * p)
  That point of the expanded design is not a realisable covariate row (a row has x*1[z=l] equal to x or 0).
  a_c is the expected response at the fitted-row means of every expanded design column (x, 1[z = l], x * 1[z = l]); the
  prior on the intercept applies to a_c. The posterior reports the raw-scale
  intercept a = a_c - sum_p mean(x_p) * b_p - sum_l p_z[l] * b_z[l] - sum_l q_x:z[l] * b_x:z[l], computed after sampling: the linear predictor at x = 0 and at the reference level.

Group effects
  none: a population-only model (no '(1 | group)' term)

Priors
  a_c ~ Normal(mu=0, sigma=5)
  b_dose ~ Normal(mu=0, sigma=2)
  b_arm[high] ~ Normal(mu=0, sigma=2)
  b_arm[low] ~ Normal(mu=0, sigma=2)
  b_dose:arm[high] ~ Normal(mu=0, sigma=1)
  b_dose:arm[low] ~ Normal(mu=0, sigma=1)
  sigma ~ HalfNormal(sigma=1)

Likelihood
  y_i ~ Normal(mu_i, sigma)

PyMC variables sampled (value space)
  sigma_log__              log(sigma)
  Intercept                a_c
  dose                     b_dose
  arm                      b_arm[high, low] (vector; dims arm_dim, posterior rows arm[high], arm[low])
  dose:arm                 b_dose:arm[high, low] (vector; dims dose:arm_dim, posterior rows dose:arm[high], dose:arm[low])
Deterministic: mu = linear predictor
